start.subtitle: Press start the moment the seizure begins. I'll guide you through what to watch for.
start.note: Works without a thermometer, scale, or watch
start.disclaimer: Disclaimer: This applet is not reviewed by, endorsed by, or affiliated with any medical professional, medical organization, or health authority.

side.text: Is the shaking happening on BOTH sides of the body?
side.sub: Look at both arms and both legs.

options.one: No — only one side or one limb

breathing_now.sub: Look for the chest or belly rising.

lips.text: What colour are the lips and face?
lips.sub: Normal skin or pink is fine. Blue or grey is serious.

still_seizing_2.sub: Are the shaking or stiffening movements still happening?

fever_visible.text: Does the child feel hot to the touch?
fever_visible.sub: Feel their forehead with the back of your hand.

breathing_rate.sub: Tap +1 breath each time the chest or belly rises.
breathing_rate.breathHelp: Tap the big button for each breath. First tap starts the 15-second timer.

breathing_effort.text: How does the breathing look right now?
breathing_effort.sub: Look for chest pulling in, noisy breaths, gasping, or long pauses.

responsiveness.text: Do they react to your voice or gentle touch at all?
responsiveness.sub: Any movement, sound, or eye opening counts.

tone.text: Does the body feel floppy or stiff?
tone.sub: Use a gentle touch only. Do not hold them down.

hands_feet.text: Do the hands and feet feel warm or cold?

post_side.text: Is one side of the body weaker than the other?
post_side.sub: Try asking the child to squeeze both your hands — is one side much weaker?

post_alert.text: Is the child starting to wake up or respond?
post_alert.sub: It is normal to be very sleepy for several minutes after a seizure.

phase0.title: Keep watching
phase0.body: Stay calm. Don't hold the child down or put anything in their mouth. Time the seizure.
actions: Keep them on their side if possible
Clear the area of hard or sharp objects
Stay with them at all times
Call 112 if this is their first ever seizure

phase1.title: Medication if available
phase1.body: If you have emergency seizure medication (prescribed by a doctor), give it now.
actions: Stay on the phone with emergency services if called

phase2.title: Emergency — call 112
phase2.body: This seizure is lasting longer than 15 minutes. Emergency services must be on the way.
actions: Do not give food or water

2min.label: ⚠ 2 minutes
2min.text: If medication is available, give it now. Keep watching the breathing.

15min.label: 🚨 15 minutes — call emergency services now
15min.text: This is a complex seizure. Call 112 immediately if you haven't already.

30min.label: 🚨 30 minutes — febrile status epilepticus
30min.text: Tell the ambulance the seizure has lasted 30 minutes. Stay on the phone with emergency services.

notBreathing.label: 🚨 Not breathing
notBreathing.text: No breaths seen. Call 112 now and start rescue breathing if trained.

breathingUnclear.label: ⚠ Breathing unclear
breathingUnclear.text: If you cannot clearly see breathing, get emergency help now and keep watching the chest and belly.

breathingConcern.label: ⚠ Breathing concern
breathingConcern.text: Breathing rate was outside usual range. Keep close watch and update emergency services.

blueLips.label: 🚨 Blue lips
blueLips.text: This is urgent. Call 112 immediately if not already done.

oneSided.label: ⚠ One-sided shaking
oneSided.text: Note this — tell the ambulance. Keep watching.

breathingEmergency.label: 🚨 Breathing emergency
breathingEmergency.text: No breaths or long pauses seen. Call 112 now and start rescue breathing if trained.

breathingHard.label: ⚠ Breathing concern
breathingHard.text: Breathing looks hard work or noisy. Keep watching closely and update emergency services.

noResponse.label: ⚠ No response
noResponse.text: No reaction to voice or touch. Keep timing the seizure and update emergency services.

summary.title: Seizure summary
summary.subtitle: For ambulance handover
summary.scriptStart: My child has had a seizure that lasted {dur}.
summary.scriptFever: They felt very hot — I think they have a fever.
summary.scriptOneSide: The shaking was only on one side of the body.
summary.scriptLittle: There was very little movement, so I could not tell whether both sides were involved.
summary.scriptNoBreath: At the early breathing check, no breathing was seen.
summary.scriptBreathUnsure: At the early breathing check, breathing was hard to confirm.
summary.scriptBreathHard: Their breathing looked hard work or noisy.
summary.scriptBreathAbsent: There were no breaths or there were long pauses in breathing.
summary.scriptNoResponse: They did not react to voice or gentle touch.
summary.scriptWeak: One side of their body seems weaker now.
summary.scriptBreathRate: Breathing rate check was about {bpm} per minute.
summary.scriptEnd: They are now in the recovery position.

side.both: Shaking on both sides of body
side.one: Shaking on ONE side only — tell ambulance
side.little: Very little movement — could not tell whether both sides were involved

breathing_now.yes: Breathing was seen at the early check
breathing_now.no: No breathing was seen at the early check

lips.blue: BLUE or grey lips — oxygen concern

fever_visible.hot: Child felt very hot — likely fever

breathing_effort.hard: Breathing looked hard work or noisy
breathing_effort.absent: No breaths or long pauses seen

responsiveness.yes: Some reaction to voice or touch
responsiveness.no: No reaction to voice or touch

hands_feet.cold: Hands and feet felt cool or cold
hands_feet.clammy: Hands and feet felt very cold or clammy

post_side.equal: Both sides equal strength after seizure
post_side.weak: One side WEAKER after seizure — tell ambulance

post_alert.yes: Child starting to wake up (normal recovery)
